head: 39d8b2e
method: batteries: every tests/*/run.sh executed serially by docs/center/generators/write_facts.py with the doctor's G3 exclusions honoured; assertions + failures parsed from each battery's own summary line, `protects` from its header comment, FIRE/SILENT from the header's own claim. hooks: probed by hand 2026-07-26 (each hook executed in a hermetic temp repo against realistic stdin payloads) — a different instrument, carried as recorded.

hooks.name: plan-proof-guard
hooks.exit_codes: PROBED, hermetic temp repos. rc=2 (the only non-zero ever observed; emitted at :132 with the ⛔ banner + Fix line on stderr :126-131) on exactly three conditions: (a) cells.exec=='done' and a `PROOF: … → … → <path>` token that resolves to nothing on disk (:112-121) — proved with proof/empty/shot.png (existing but EMPTY dir) and proof/never/shot.png; (b) cells.red=='done' with an empty/absent `cases` string (:103-106); (c) cells.red=='done' whose cases cite `red@<sha>` unreachable via `git cat-file -e <sha>^{commit}` (:108-110). Fires identically for file_path ending .kdbp/PLAN.md as for .kdbp/PLAN.json (:22). rc=0 on all 18 other probed inputs: no .kdbp/PLAN.json (:16); non-plan file_path (:21-24); payload with no file_path key; garbage stdin; empty stdin; python3 absent (:27-30, prints `[WARN] plan-proof-guard INERT: python3 not on PATH — PLAN honesty checks were NOT run` to stderr); malformed PLAN.json (:86-89); proof string containing no '→' (:114); proof that is a LIST not a str (:114); proof segment with <3 arrow parts (:117); segment not starting with 'PROOF' (:117); cells.exec=='DONE' (case-sensitive compare at :112); red done with a cases record citing no sha (:108); phases as a string; phases containing null; and any payload whose FIRST `"file_path"` in raw JSON text is not the plan. rc=1 never observed. Timing (matters against timeout 10): a 64,000-candidate 3-level brace token → rc=2 in 27ms (MAX_BRACE 256 cap, :35,:41); 300 distinct unreachable shas → rc=2 in 340ms.
hooks.reads: `.kdbp/PLAN.json` resolved RELATIVE TO THE HOOK'S CWD (:16 existence test, :87 json.load) — it never reads the file that was actually written and never reads PLAN.md despite matching on it. Per phase it reads only phases[].cells.red, phases[].cells.exec, phases[].cases, phases[].proof (:100-121). Also reads: the filesystem via os.path.exists / glob.glob / os.listdir (:64-84), and git via `git cat-file -e` subprocesses (:96). From stdin it extracts ONLY the first `"file_path": "…"` string by grep (:20) — no JSON parse of the hook payload. In the suite repo itself there is no .kdbp/ (CLAUDE.md ruling R8), so :16 short-circuits and the hook is unconditionally silent here; it is live in the operator's ~/.claude/settings.json (PostToolUse, matcher Write|Edit|MultiEdit, timeout 10) and only bites in downstream KDBP projects.
hooks.fail_open: Ten proven paths, five of which the script's own header does not list. (1) .kdbp/PLAN.json absent → rc=0 (:16): a project carrying only PLAN.md with ✅ rows is completely unguarded — probed rc=0 against exactly that. Since PLAN.json is produced by the model-invoked regen-mirror.py, deleting or never generating the mirror disables the suite's only blocking mechanism. (2) python3 absent → rc=0 with a warn line (:27-30). (3) malformed PLAN.json → rc=0 (:86-89, deliberate). (4) PYTHON CRASH IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A PASS: the heredoc at :32 carries `2>/dev/null` and the shell has `set -uo pipefail` with NO `-e`, so a TypeError leaves `viol` empty and the hook exits 0 — probed with phases as a string and with phases:[null], both rc=0, no output, no warning. (5) sha_cache 200-entry cap (:94 `if len(sha_cache) >= 200: return True`) — EMPIRICALLY EXPLOITED: a plan with 200 reachable shas plus one `red@deadbeefdeadbeef` exits 0, while the same fake sha alone exits 2. Past-cap lies pass unverified. (6) `proof` not a str, or a str without '→' (:114) → the exec⇒proof invariant silently does not run. (7) a proof segment whose first arrow-part does not upper-start with 'PROOF' (:117) → skipped. (8) <3 arrow parts → skipped (:117). (9) cells value 'Done'/'DONE' → the =='done' compare at :103/:112 misses it. (10) the path test greps the FIRST `"file_path"` in the raw payload text (:20) — a payload whose first file_path is a decoy (e.g. a tool_response emitted before tool_input) exits 0 without checking anything; conversely any file_path merely ENDING in `.kdbp/PLAN.json` (a DIFFERENT project's plan) triggers a full check of the LOCAL plan and can block on the local plan's violations — both probed. Structural: PostToolUse fires AFTER the write lands, so a dishonest PLAN.json is already on disk; this is blocking feedback, never write prevention (the header says so at :12).
hooks.fixture_coverage: tests/hooks/run.sh:43-66 — 17 assertions, the ONLY hook whose exit code the battery actually asserts (helper `guard_on()` :30-37 echoes `$?`; :63-66 capture `$?` directly). BOTH DIRECTIONS PROVEN. FIRE (rc=2) at :47 empty evidence dir, :48 missing dir, :49 bare `*`, :50 `../../**`, :51 mid-path brace with no real alternative (round-5 CRITICAL), :57 red done without cases, :59 unreachable sha. SILENT (rc=0) at :43 literal path, :44 trailing '(4 shots)' annotation, :45 `01..06-*.png` range, :46 brace shorthand, :53 cap-tripped multi-brace with real evidence (round-4 false-block regression), :54 proof:null, :58 reachable sha, :60 cases without a sha, :64 non-plan write, :66 garbage stdin. NOT COVERED — every fail-open enumerated above except the two stdin ones: no fixture for the python3-absent INERT path, malformed PLAN.json, the swallowed python crash, the 200-sha cache cap (I proved it exploitable), proof-not-a-string, a segment missing the PROOF prefix, a PLAN.md-only project, or the first-file_path-wins path selection. Battery verified green this session: 47 passed / 0 failed.
hooks.discrepancy: Header :2 declares the hook is 'for Write|Edit on .kdbp/PLAN.json / PLAN.md' while the shipped wiring matcher is `Write|Edit|MultiEdit` (templates/hooks.json:58) — the header understates its own surface. Header :5 promises it 'validates the WHOLE current PLAN.json state after the write', but 'current' means the CWD's plan while the trigger accepts any path suffixed `.kdbp/PLAN.json|PLAN.md`, so the file examined and the file written need not be the same file (probed: `/some/other/project/.kdbp/PLAN.json` blocked on local violations). Header :12-13 accounts for only ONE fail-open ('parse errors exit 0'); it omits the sha-cache cap, the swallowed python crash, the proof-shape misses, and the PLAN.md-only blind spot. Everything else in the header is accurate — exit 2 + stderr, the R2 leniency ladder, and the two honesty rules all behave as written.

hooks.name: pre-checkpoint
hooks.exit_codes: PROBED rc=0 on EVERY path — 25+ variants, no non-zero ever observed. rc=0 with output on: plain `git commit` (:37-38); `echo "building" && git commit` ; `; git commit`; a newline-separated `cd x\ngit commit` (grep is line-anchored); a staged NEW test file with no C-id (:42-52); a declared C-id with 0 corpus hits (:66-72); a staged test file chmod 000 (grep rc=2 inverted by `if !` at :49 → false-warn, fail-loud). rc=0 SILENT on: no .kdbp/BEHAVIOR.md (:8, stdin never consumed); `npm test`; `git log --grep "; git commit"` (shlex-balanced quote stripping, :26-29); garbage stdin; empty stdin; malformed .kdbp/PLAN.json (:64 `except Exception: pass`); a KDBP dir that is not a git repo. This hook sits in the ONE slot where a non-zero exit has hard power — PreToolUse exit 2 aborts the Bash call — and it structurally never returns one, so its slot privilege is unused.
hooks.reads: `.kdbp/BEHAVIOR.md` EXISTENCE only (:8) — its contents are never opened, unlike session-kdbp-active which parses it. stdin: `tool_input.command` via a real `json.load` + `shlex.split` balance test + quoted-span stripping (:19-32), with a raw grep fallback at :35 when python3 is absent. Then: `git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=A -z` (:52) for staged NEW files, each such file's CONTENTS when its path matches `(^|/)tests?/|(^|/)test_[^/]+\.|\.(test|spec)\.[a-zA-Z]+$` (:44,:49), `.kdbp/PLAN.json` current_phase + that phase's `cases` string (:56-65), and `git grep -qE` over the repo excluding `.kdbp` (:69). Inert in the suite repo (no .kdbp/, CLAUDE.md R8); live in ~/.claude/settings.json.
hooks.fail_open: NINE proven silent misses of the raw-commit trigger, all rc=0 with zero output. The regex at :37 is `(^|&&[[:space:]]*|;[[:space:]]*)git commit`, so it misses: `  git commit -m x` (LEADING WHITESPACE — the most plausible real form, `^` admits no indent); `true || git commit`; `true | git commit`; `(git commit -m x)`; `{ git commit -m x; }`; `if true; then git commit -m x; fi` (the `; ` is followed by `then`, not `git`); `git -C . commit`; `sudo git commit`; `env FOO=1 git commit`. Separately, the no-python3 fallback at :34-36 REINTRODUCES the exact round-3 truncation bug the python parser was written to fix: with python3 hidden on PATH, `echo "building" && git commit -m x` produces NO warning at all (probed), because `grep -o '"command"…"[^"]*"'` stops at the first escaped quote. Plain `git commit` still warns on that path, so the degradation is partial and invisible. Also: the C-id and declared-case warn classes are nested INSIDE the raw-commit trigger (:37-74), so every one of the nine misses above also silently skips both D7 debt checks — a commit made via `/gabe-commit` or any unmatched form is never inspected for C-ids at all.
hooks.fixture_coverage: tests/hooks/run.sh:70-74 (5 assertions — plain commit WARNs, commit-after-a-quoted-arg WARNs, unterminated-quote typo still WARNs, quoted data stays silent, `npm test` stays silent), :82-84 (3 — spaced filename without an id WARNs, the SEC101 decoy does not satisfy the id check, a C147 file does NOT warn), :92 and :95 (2 — declared C999 with 0 hits WARNs, declared C147 present does NOT). 10 assertions; both FIRE and SILENT proven for STDOUT CONTENT. THE EXIT CODE IS NEVER ASSERTED: helper `pre()` at :69 pipes the hook's stdout into `grep -c` (discarding `$?`), and the three `out=$(… | bash "$PRE" 2>/dev/null)` captures at :81/:91/:94 discard it too. A `set -euo pipefail` regression turning this PreToolUse hook non-zero would ABORT EVERY BASH CALL in every KDBP project and the battery would still print 47/47 green. Also uncovered: all nine missed separator forms, and the entire no-python3 fallback branch (where I proved a real false-silence).
hooks.discrepancy: Header :16 states the design guarantee as 'false-warn over false-silence; a parity count cannot make that guarantee' — but the grep fallback it introduces one line earlier (':16 Grep fallback (raw, unstripped) when python3 is absent', implemented at :35) is itself a false-SILENCE path, proved above. Header :4 ('never blocks — debts warn; only plan-proof-guard blocks lies') is accurate and matches rc=0 on every probe. Header :5-6 describes both warn classes accurately.

hooks.name: post-structure-warning
hooks.exit_codes: PROBED rc=0 on every path, no non-zero ever observed. rc=0 with output (`[INFO] STRUCTURE: new file <path> — verify placement matches .kdbp/STRUCTURE.md`, :13) for ANY tool_name=='Write' whose relativized path does not begin with `.kdbp/`, `node_modules/` or `.git/` — regardless of whether that path matches anything in STRUCTURE.md. rc=0 SILENT on: no .kdbp/STRUCTURE.md (:5, stdin never consumed); tool_name != Write (:8); a `.kdbp/…` path; an EXISTING `node_modules/pkg/x.js`; a `.git/config` path; garbage stdin; empty stdin; a Write payload with no file_path key (:10). PostToolUse exit 2 would be blocking feedback here — it never returns one, and there is no code path that could.
hooks.reads: `.kdbp/STRUCTURE.md` EXISTENCE ONLY (:5, `[ -f ]`) — the file is never opened, never parsed, and its allowed-pattern table is never consulted. From stdin, by grep: `tool_name` (:7) and `tool_input.file_path` (:9). Then `realpath --relative-to="$(pwd)"` (:11) and one hardcoded exclusion regex `^(\.kdbp/|node_modules/|\.git/)` (:12). Inert in the suite repo (no .kdbp/).
hooks.fail_open: Structurally total: the hook evaluates NO rule, so it can neither pass nor fail a placement — a file that perfectly matches a STRUCTURE.md pattern and a file that violates every pattern produce the identical INFO line (probed both). Concretely also: the hardcoded exclusion is defeated whenever `realpath --relative-to` fails, because :11 falls back to `echo "$file_path"` (the raw ABSOLUTE path), which cannot match the `^node_modules/` anchor — probed: a Write to `<repo>/node_modules/ghost/y.js` whose parent dir does not yet exist FIRES with the full absolute path, while `<repo>/node_modules/pkg/x.js` (parent exists) stays silent. Same fallback makes a write ABOVE the cwd print `../outside.py`. Nothing consumes the INFO line either — it is stdout from a PostToolUse hook with no downstream reader.
hooks.fixture_coverage: tests/hooks/run.sh:123-128 — 3 assertions: FIRE (`po` on a Write to src/stray.py must print 'STRUCTURE: new file src/stray.py', :123-124), SILENT on a `.kdbp/` write (:125-126), SILENT on a non-Write tool (:127-128). FIRE and SILENT are both proven, but ONLY for the hardcoded prefix exclusion — no fixture ever writes a pattern into .kdbp/STRUCTURE.md and asserts that a CONFORMING file stays silent, because the script is incapable of that and such a fixture would fail. So the battery certifies the behavior while the header and templates/CLAUDE.md advertise a different one. Exit code never asserted: helper `po()` at :121 captures stdout only. The realpath-degradation path (`node_modules/<missing-dir>/…` fires) is uncovered.
hooks.discrepancy: BROKEN CLAIM, two carriers. (1) The script's OWN header, :3: 'Warns when a new file is created outside allowed patterns in .kdbp/STRUCTURE.md'. The script never opens .kdbp/STRUCTURE.md; :5 tests existence and :12 applies three hardcoded directory prefixes. There are no 'allowed patterns' in the code. (2) templates/CLAUDE.md:42, shipped verbatim into every downstream project: '3. **STRUCTURE before placement.** New files must match a pattern in `.kdbp/STRUCTURE.md` — PostToolUse hook warns on drift.' The hook cannot detect drift; it announces every new file identically. A third, smaller mismatch: templates/CLAUDE.md:21 attributes STRUCTURE enforcement to 'gabe-commit CHECK 9', but the shipped gate spec numbers that check CHECK 8 (skills/gabe-commit/references/gate-spec.md:128 '**CHECK 8 — Structure**') — the downstream-facing pointer names a check number that does not exist.

hooks.name: session-kdbp-active
hooks.exit_codes: PROBED. rc=0 + `[INFO] KDBP Active — <name> (<maturity>) [<tech>]` when .kdbp/BEHAVIOR.md carries all three keys (:9). rc=0 SILENT when .kdbp/BEHAVIOR.md is absent (:5). rc=1 SILENT — NO OUTPUT AT ALL — whenever .kdbp/BEHAVIOR.md EXISTS but is missing any one of `^name:`, `^maturity:` or `^tech:`. I probed all four failure shapes (missing name / missing maturity / missing tech / empty file) and every one returned rc=1 with empty stdout and stderr. Cause: `set -euo pipefail` at :4 plus a failing `grep` inside the command substitutions at :6, :7 and :8 — the script dies before reaching the echo at :9. SessionStart exit codes are INERT (the harness surfaces the error to the user but neither blocks nor feeds the model), so rc=1 is a silent loss of the announcement, not a gate.
hooks.reads: `.kdbp/BEHAVIOR.md` only, three grep-anchored lines: `^name:` (:6), `^maturity:` (:7), `^tech:` (:8). Never reads stdin — the SessionStart hook JSON is discarded entirely (no `cat`). Inert in the suite repo (no .kdbp/, CLAUDE.md R8); live in ~/.claude/settings.json as SessionStart matcher `*` timeout 5.
hooks.fail_open: There is no fail-open in the enforcement sense, because there is nothing to enforce — the hook only announces. The inverse defect is what exists: a FAIL-CLOSED-AND-SILENT path. Any BEHAVIOR.md that a downstream project hand-edits into an incomplete state turns this hook into a mute rc=1 crash for every session start, with no diagnostic, and no other hook notices (pre-checkpoint and stop-session-reminder only test the file's EXISTENCE, so they keep firing normally against the same broken file).
hooks.fixture_coverage: tests/hooks/run.sh:130-131 — exactly 1 assertion: FIRE only (a complete BEHAVIOR.md must print `KDBP Active — Fixture (mvp) [bash]`). SILENT is proven only indirectly, folded into the shared non-KDBP-dir assertion at :141-142 which runs this hook plus stop-session-reminder plus session-plan-awareness in one temp dir and asserts combined empty output. The exit code is never asserted — :130 pipes the hook into `grep -q`, discarding `$?`. NOTHING covers the rc=1 crash path: no fixture writes an incomplete BEHAVIOR.md. Thinnest coverage of the six.
hooks.discrepancy: Header :3: 'Shows KDBP status when .kdbp/ exists in the working directory' — probed false for any incomplete BEHAVIOR.md, where it shows nothing and exits 1. This also contradicts the prior audit's characterization at audit_raw.md:247 ('Print-only; missing keys degrade to blank/`?` rather than failing'); the CORRECTION at audit_raw.md:889 already reversed that for `name:`/`maturity:`, and I additionally confirmed the same rc=1 for a missing `tech:` line and for a zero-byte BEHAVIOR.md. Note also this is the only one of the six hooks whose non-zero exit is NOT a deliberate signal — it is an uncaught `set -e` abort.

hooks.name: session-plan-awareness
hooks.exit_codes: PROBED rc=0 on every path, no non-zero ever observed. rc=0 with output: active mirror → `[INFO] ACTIVE PLAN: Phase 1 — Fix (exec:done review:todo commit:todo push:todo)` (:22); non-active status → `none — run /gabe-plan to create one` (:15); malformed PLAN.json + a PLAN.md carrying a 🔄 row → `in progress — 🔄 Doing it` (:39); PLAN.md `^No active plan` → `none` (:35); PLAN.md with neither → `present — check .kdbp/PLAN.md` (:41); current_phase pointing at a nonexistent phase → `Phase 9 — check .kdbp/PLAN.md` (:24). rc=0 SILENT: no .kdbp at all; PLAN.json present + python3 ABSENT + no PLAN.md (probed — total silence). SessionStart exit codes are inert regardless.
hooks.reads: `.kdbp/PLAN.json` via python3 (:6-25): `status`, `current_phase`, and for the matching phase `name` plus `cells.{exec,review,commit,push}`. Falls back to `.kdbp/PLAN.md` (:33-43): the literal line `^No active plan` (:34) and the first `^| [0-9A-Z]` table row containing 🔄, third pipe-field extracted by awk (:37-39). Inert in the suite repo (no .kdbp/).
hooks.fail_open: (1) PLAN.json present + python3 missing + no PLAN.md → completely silent rc=0 (probed): the session loses plan awareness with no diagnostic whatsoever. Contrast plan-proof-guard :27-30, which prints an explicit `INERT` warning for the same missing dependency — the two hooks make opposite choices about announcing their own incapacity. (2) A malformed PLAN.json is swallowed at :7 (`2>/dev/null || true` + SystemExit(1) at :12) and silently downgraded to the prose file, so a corrupt mirror is invisible here even though next.mjs treats the same file as an exit-2 refusal. (3) A `current_phase` that resolves to no phase prints a cheerful `Phase 9 — …` (:24) rather than surfacing the desync that next.mjs exits 2 on. (4) No `.kdbp/BEHAVIOR.md` gate — probed: the hook announces in ANY directory holding a `.kdbp/PLAN.md`, whether or not the project was ever /gabe-init'd, which is the opposite gating from the other five hooks.
hooks.fixture_coverage: tests/hooks/run.sh:134 (active mirror summarizes the phase), :136 (non-active mirror says none), :139 (PLAN.md 'No active plan' fallback says none) = 3 assertions, plus the shared non-KDBP silence at :141-142. FIRE and SILENT both represented, but only for the happy mirror paths. Exit code never asserted — helper `spa()` at :132 is piped into `grep -q`. UNCOVERED: the python3-absent silent hole, a malformed PLAN.json, the current_phase desync, the 🔄-row PLAN.md branch (:37-39, the only branch with awk field extraction), and the missing red/center cells.
hooks.discrepancy: Header :3 ('Shows current plan status from .kdbp/PLAN.json (machine mirror), falling back to .kdbp/PLAN.md') is accurate for the paths it names but omits the silent no-python3 hole. Substantive drift against the current plan schema: the cells trail printed at :21 is hardcoded to `("exec", "review", "commit", "push")` and therefore omits BOTH columns the verification-first work added — `red` and `center` — so the SessionStart announcement cannot show whether a phase is red-checkpointed, which is precisely the state plan-proof-guard blocks on.

hooks.name: stop-session-reminder
hooks.exit_codes: PROBED rc=0 on every path, no non-zero ever observed. rc=0 with output (`\nnext: /gabe-commit (<n> tracked file(s) dirty, no commit this session)`, :27-28) on: dirty tree + HEAD older than 1800s + no transcript_path; dirty tree + a transcript that exists but lacks the string `git commit`; dirty tree + a transcript_path pointing at a nonexistent file; a git repo with NO commits at all and a staged file (`git log -1` fails → `|| echo 0` at :23 → head_age ≈ epoch). rc=0 SILENT on: clean tree (:13); untracked-only dirt (:12 filters `^??`); no .kdbp/BEHAVIOR.md (:8); not inside a git work tree (:9); dirty + HEAD younger than 1800s with no transcript (:24); a transcript containing `git commit` (:19-20); garbage stdin; empty stdin; python3 absent (unused). Stop exit 2 would BLOCK the session from stopping — this hook has no code path that returns it.
hooks.reads: `.kdbp/BEHAVIOR.md` existence only (:8). `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` (:9). `git status --porcelain` with `^??` lines excluded, counted (:12). From stdin, by grep: `transcript_path` (:17). If that path exists, it greps THE ENTIRE TRANSCRIPT FILE for the literal substring `git commit` (:19). Otherwise `git log -1 --format=%ct` compared against a hardcoded 1800s (:23-24). Inert in the suite repo (no .kdbp/).
hooks.fail_open: The 'no commit landed this session' test is a bare substring grep and fails in BOTH directions, both probed. FALSE SILENCE: any transcript merely CONTAINING the text `git commit` suppresses the reminder — I proved it with a transcript whose only content is pre-checkpoint's own warn line `[WARN] KDBP CHECKPOINT: Use /gabe-commit instead of raw git commit`, and again with a transcript that only discusses git commit in prose. So the sibling hook's output silences this one. FALSE FIRE: when transcript_path resolves to an existing file, the `else` branch at :22-25 is skipped entirely, so the HEAD-age guard never runs — I proved the reminder fires with a HEAD committed seconds earlier, purely because the transcript text lacked the phrase. Additional: a repo with zero commits always fires; a nonexistent transcript_path falls to the age branch silently.
hooks.fixture_coverage: tests/hooks/run.sh:112 (FIRE: dirty tree + old HEAD + no transcript prints the routing line, M24), :114 (SILENT: transcript containing a commit), :116 (SILENT: clean tree), :118 (SILENT: untracked-only dirt) = 4 assertions, plus the shared non-KDBP silence at :141-142. BOTH FIRE AND SILENT ARE PROVEN. Exit code never asserted — helper `so()` at :111 captures stdout only. UNCOVERED: the transcript branch bypassing the HEAD-age guard (the false-fire I proved), the substring false-positive (a transcript containing only the phrase, not a real commit), the nonexistent-transcript_path path, and the zero-commit repo.
hooks.discrepancy: Header :3: 'Fires ONLY when: KDBP project AND working tree dirty AND no commit landed this session.' The third condition is not implemented as commit detection — it is a substring grep over a transcript file (:19), with a documented-in-comment 30-minute HEAD-age approximation (:22-24) that is BYPASSED whenever a transcript is supplied. Both a false silence and a false fire were reproduced against that sentence. Header :4 ('Prints a single deterministic next-step line. Zero model memory, no other reminders.') is accurate.

Proves, hermetically on a synthetic center (a c4-graph.json carrying the emitter's `models` block, in a temp dir): * FIRE — every declared verdict is projected with its why + suggested edit; every CANDIDATE arrives NAMED (the emitter's name, `named_by` domain|table, a suggested slug, `draft_name()`'s action phrase). * SILENT — an all-FEATURE, no-candidate block → a VALID EMPTY draft (candidates []), so a stale one never lingers. * HONEST-EMPTY — no center config · no c4 · unreadable c4 · no `models` block → the reason printed, NOTHING written, exit 0. * DETERMINISM — a second run on an unchanged input writes nothing ("unchanged") and is byte-identical; the c4 head is the only stamp. * ABSTAIN — a witnessless atom lands in `abstained`, never in `candidates`; `coverage.witnessed` is present and right. * PROJECTION — the draft's declared verdicts EQUAL the block's proposed roster (nothing derived locally) — the mutation "derive a verdict here" reddens it; flipping the fixture's anchor table changes the fallback name. * --min · --model derived · R10 (no "orphan"). Exit 0 = all pass.

batteries.name: workflow-drafts
batteries.protects: draft-workflows.py fixture battery — the curate-workflows DRAFTER's executable contract (operator ruling 2026-09-04: journey creation becomes a suite step). Proves, hermetically on a synthetic center (c4-graph.json + workflows.js in a temp dir): * FIRE — uncovered endpoints reached from a screen become ONE draft per entity·screen cluster, steps ordered read→write, level SUGGESTED (no writes → 1 · single-entity writes → 2 · cross-entity → 3), `draft:true`, named from the screen + verb phrase. * SILENT — every endpoint covered by workflows.js → zero drafts (an EMPTY draft file, so a stale draft never lingers). * HONEST-EMPTY — no center config → the reason printed, NOTHING written, exit 0; no c4 → same. * UNREACHED — an uncovered endpoint no screen calls is REPORTED, never drafted (a bridge gap or a dead endpoint is the human's call). * INFRA — BOOT events and `/_…` paths are skipped by idiom, counted, never drafted. * DETERMINISM — a second run on an unchanged input writes nothing and is byte-identical. * MUTATION — remove the write op → the suggested level drops 2→1 (the level is READ from the graph). * TOLERANT PARSE — a `{param}` inside a curated step label does not break coverage. Exit 0 = all pass.

scripts/hooks/kdbp/pre-checkpoint.sh EXIT CODE — a coverage HOLE inside an otherwise-green battery rather than a missing battery. tests/hooks/run.sh:69 defines `pre() { printf '%s' "$1" | bash "$PRE" 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'KDBP CHECKPOINT'; }` — the hook's rc is discarded by the pipe, and every one of the 11 pre-checkpoint assertions (:70-95) tests stdout content only. Because this is a PreToolUse hook on Bash, a regression making it exit non-zero would interfere with `git commit` in every KDBP project and this battery would still report 47 passed / 0 failed.

templates/hooks.json's own shape — no validator and no battery. It is the six-marker object (`KDBP Active`, `ACTIVE PLAN`, `KDBP CHECKPOINT`, `STRUCTURE:`, `PLAN-PROOF-GUARD`, `SESSION-END REMINDER`) that /gabe-init copies verbatim into ~/.claude/settings.json; the doctor only byte-compares repo vs install, and skills/gabe-init/references/init-spec.md tells the model to STOP rather than improvise if a key is missing. A malformed or wrongly-keyed entry would install silently.
